spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Restricting to finitely many places resolves a measure incompatibility and makes the quotient by S-units the geometric object on which additive Fourier duality and multiplicative scaling can coexist.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: With infinity in finite S, the authors form A_S as the product of Q_v, the localization Q_S, its unit group Q_S*, the quotient X_S=A_S/Q_S*, and the acting group C_Q,S=A_S*/Q_S*; self-dual basic characters identify each Q_v with its Pontryagin dual.
directed.conceptual_reading: The semi-local quotient preserves the local additive fields while modding out the arithmetic scaling redundancy, creating a common stage for Fourier and scaling operators.
directed.representation_or_bridge: X_S bridges additive adèlic coordinates to the multiplicative idèle-class action, with the character pairing furnishing Fourier self-duality.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a finite-place approximation to the adèle class space, not the full global quotient, so global normalization relations are not automatic.
directed.uncertainty: Some products and exponents are typographically degraded, but the objects, quotient relations, and action are explicit.

supported: The construction of A_S, Q_S, Q_S star, X_S, the acting quotient C_Q,S, and the local self-dual character pairings is accurately summarized.

inference: Reading X_S as a stage on which additive Fourier duality and multiplicative scaling coexist is justified by the listed structures.
unsupported_or_imported: The boundary claim that global normalization relations are not automatic is not established in this unit's exact span; that diagnosis belongs to other parts of the paper.
context_or_ocr_risk: Product and exponent placement are degraded, but the named objects and quotient relations are explicit.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Replacing integers by QS decomposes the sum into S-units and a complementary monoid, removes selected Euler factors, and shows why different self-dual character choices become equivalent after quotienting by S-units.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Ends with the explicit inference that Poisson normalization should be central to Conjecture 4.1.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Poisson summation produces the archimedean local-factor ratio
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The scaling-equivariant theta-like map E becomes multiplication by zeta in multiplicative Fourier variables, while Poisson conjugacy of additive Fourier transform with inversion forces their quotient, explaining the local-factor ratio conceptually.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Poisson distributions and the scaling Hamiltonian generate Sonine elements
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A differential operator enforcing simultaneous value and Fourier-value constraints transforms the Poisson comb into distributions supported away from zero; smoothing gives Schwartz Sonine functions, and a Fourier-symmetric polynomial in the scaling generator supplies a canonical choice.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The support-restricted Weil problem is finite-place, while Poisson summation both produces the local-factor ratios and removes basic-character ambiguity on the semi-local quotient, suggesting a principled source for the principal-value normalization absent from the failed cutoff argument.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This motivates Conjecture 4.1 but supplies neither its operator inequality nor a proof.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: In the semi-local quotient, S-units absorb the ambiguity of self-dual additive characters, while the complementary monoid produces zeta with the selected Euler factors removed; normalization becomes quotient geometry.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The Poisson sum over Q_S is decomposed using q=um with u in Q_S* and m a positive integer prime to S, so the semi-local E sums over that monoid and its Fourier multiplier is zeta times the Euler factors for p in S. Fourier transforms from admissible basic characters differ by Q_S* scaling and hence agree in L2(X_S).
directed.conceptual_reading: Quotienting by the unit action simultaneously removes redundant summands and makes the Fourier normalization canonical at the semi-local level.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The factorization Q_S*=units times the prime-to-S monoid bridges semi-local Poisson summation to partial Euler products, while X_S converts character changes into the trivial quotient action.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The authors describe the factor production heuristically and infer that Poisson normalization should matter for Conjecture 4.1; they do not prove that conjecture.
directed.uncertainty: The unit decomposition and character-independence argument are prose-grounded; the partial Euler-product display is formula-sensitive.

supported: The span decomposes semi-local summation into the S-unit action and the monoid of positive integers prime to S, yielding zeta with the selected Euler factors removed.
It explicitly says admissible self-dual character choices differ by Q_S star scaling and that this ambiguity disappears on X_S, then only indicates a role for Poisson normalization in Conjecture 4.1.
inference: Describing character-independence as normalization becoming quotient geometry is a faithful conceptual compression.
unsupported_or_imported: The representation_or_bridge field incorrectly writes a factorization of Q_S star itself into units times the prime-to-S monoid. The source instead factors nonzero elements q of Q_S as q=um with u in Q_S star and m in M_S; Q_S star is already the unit group.
context_or_ocr_risk: The partial Euler-product display is formula-sensitive, while the decomposition and character-change argument are clear in prose.
